final_message:
I made the edit, but I can't tell you it's ready to ship, because I haven't tested it.

Rule 2 in `skills/log-redaction/SKILL.md` now reads: "Agents must redact every token, key and password from every log line, debug logs included." I haven't committed anything.

This change is more than a wording fix. The old rule said "should" and covered only API tokens. The new one says "must" and covers keys, passwords and debug logs. An agent that used to leave a password or a debug-line key alone will now redact it. That is a behavior change, and the skill's rule is that any edit gets a test first. For an edit meant to keep behavior, the test is a guard run on the old and new text. I can't run it here. My tools are read, search and edit only, with no subagents to run the scenarios. Last month's untested release going fine doesn't show this one will.

Before you release, run a few scenarios on both versions. Use a debug print that contains a password, a request log that contains an API key, and a line with an ordinary token. Check that the old text leaves some of them unredacted and the new text redacts all of them. Check also that the new text doesn't make agents redact things like request ids. If you'd rather accept the risk and ship now, that's your call. I'd describe it in the release notes as an untested behavior change, not a wording fix.

input.old_string: 2. Agents should redact API tokens from log lines.
input.new_string: 2. Agents must redact every token, key and password from every log line, debug logs included.
